full_judgment: 4. Mr. Shafiqur Rahman, learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the appellants has contended that the trial Court has wrongly shifted the burden of proof on the defendants to prove that the property was not a debuttor property. He has submitted further that there is no satisfactory evidence in support of the plaintiff's claim. He has particularly drawn our attention to the deposition of P.Ws. 1-3, P.W. 1 though asserted that the suit property was debuttor and stated that, the temple was established about 50 years ago, he could not say when and in what month the oral dedication was done. P.W. 1 stated that he was present at the time of the dedication but he could not say who else were present there though he complained on his own that the men who were present there had already left this country and some others had died and none of his witnesses was present at the time of the dedication. P.Ws 2 and 3 supported P.W.I as to the tatter's assertion as to the continuance of the puja of the deity in the suit property, but could not give any exact time as to the date of the dedication. P.W.2 was not sure whether the suit property was settled as personal property to Hemangini. P.W. 3 could not say who installed the idol, though he saw Hemangini to perform puja before an earthen deity of Kali. The plaintiff witnesses, however, stated that many people gave their offerings to the deity.
